Detailed Instructions: Confirm that version 1 contains a start-page table, create/edit/delete operations, a detail card, Markdown content, examples, images, and English/German/Russian content.
Acceptance Criteria: The MVP contains every requested function and excludes optional post-MVP features.

Detailed Instructions: Use one repository with a React SPA, Spring Boot REST API, PostgreSQL database, local image storage, and Docker Compose.
Acceptance Criteria: Architecture and top-level directories are agreed.

Detailed Instructions: Require a unique slug, translations for EN/DE/RU, valid content, optional ordered images, passing tests, and a successful clean-start smoke test.
Acceptance Criteria: A concise definition of done is documented.

Detailed Instructions: Install Git in WSL and configure the developer name and email when not already configured.
Commands / Files: git --version; git config --global user.name; git config --global user.email
Acceptance Criteria: git --version succeeds inside WSL.

Detailed Instructions: Install a Java 21 JDK inside WSL and configure JAVA_HOME if required.
Acceptance Criteria: Both commands report Java 21.

Detailed Instructions: Install Docker Desktop with WSL integration or Docker Engine in WSL, including Docker Compose.
Commands / Files: docker --version; docker compose version; docker run --rm hello-world
Acceptance Criteria: Docker commands work from the Ubuntu WSL shell.

Detailed Instructions: Install the current supported Node.js LTS in WSL using a version manager and pin the selected version.
Acceptance Criteria: Node and npm work in WSL and .nvmrc pins the version.

Detailed Instructions: Use a Windows editor with WSL integration and install Java, Spring, TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, and Tailwind extensions.
Commands / Files: Editor WSL extension and project settings
Acceptance Criteria: The repository opens in WSL mode with working terminals and language services.

Detailed Instructions: Review existing files, Git state, and repository instructions before scaffolding; preserve unrelated work.
Acceptance Criteria: Existing files and constraints are understood and preserved.

Detailed Instructions: Initialize Git if necessary and create backend, frontend, docs, and uploads directories plus a root README.
Commands / Files: git init; backend/; frontend/; docs/; uploads/; README.md
Acceptance Criteria: The agreed repository structure exists.

Detailed Instructions: Ignore secrets, IDE files, node_modules, Java build output, uploads, logs, and local database data while retaining required empty directories.
Acceptance Criteria: Generated or sensitive files do not appear in Git status.

Detailed Instructions: Create a Maven Spring Boot application using Java 21 with Web, Data JPA, Validation, PostgreSQL, Flyway, and Actuator.
Acceptance Criteria: ./mvnw test starts the Spring context successfully.

Detailed Instructions: Create configuration, controller, service, repository, domain, DTO, mapper, storage, and exception packages.
Acceptance Criteria: The package structure is clear and the application compiles.

Detailed Instructions: Create default, local, and test configuration; read database, CORS, and upload settings from environment variables.
Acceptance Criteria: Local and test profiles start without committed credentials.

Detailed Instructions: Define a health-checked PostgreSQL service with a named volume and local development credentials in Docker Compose.
Acceptance Criteria: The database container becomes healthy and accepts connections.

Detailed Instructions: Design element, element_translation, and element_image records with timestamps, language codes, image order, and cascading rules.
Acceptance Criteria: The model supports EN, DE, RU and future languages without duplicating elements.

Detailed Instructions: Create tables, indexes, foreign keys, check constraints, and uniqueness for slug and element/language pairs.
Acceptance Criteria: Migration applies successfully to an empty PostgreSQL database.

Detailed Instructions: Create at least two representative IT definitions with complete translations and examples for local development.
Commands / Files: Local-only seed migration or profile-specific initializer
Acceptance Criteria: The API can be demonstrated immediately after local startup.

Detailed Instructions: Implement Element, ElementTranslation, and ElementImage with audit timestamps and carefully chosen cascade/orphan behavior.
Acceptance Criteria: Entities persist and reload all translations and ordered images.

Detailed Instructions: Create Spring Data repositories and efficient list/detail queries that avoid unnecessary repeated queries.
Acceptance Criteria: Repository tests cover save, query, uniqueness, and deletion.

Detailed Instructions: Create separate list, detail, create/update, translation, image, and validation-error DTOs; never expose entities directly.
Acceptance Criteria: The HTTP contract contains all required fields and no persistence internals.

Detailed Instructions: Require a valid unique slug and nonblank EN/DE/RU translations; validate text lengths, image type/size, and display order.
Acceptance Criteria: Invalid requests return HTTP 400 with field-level errors.

Detailed Instructions: Add transactional list, read, create, update, and delete methods; normalize slugs and define not-found/duplicate behavior.
Acceptance Criteria: Service tests cover successful and exceptional paths.

Detailed Instructions: Expose GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/elements and GET /api/elements/{id}; use correct HTTP statuses and Location on creation.
Acceptance Criteria: All element operations work through HTTP.

Detailed Instructions: Add centralized handling for validation, malformed input, missing records, conflicts, large uploads, and unexpected errors.
Acceptance Criteria: Errors have a stable machine-readable structure and no stack traces.

Detailed Instructions: Use an uploads directory outside the packaged application, generate safe server filenames, and block path traversal.
Acceptance Criteria: Files cannot be written outside the configured directory.

Detailed Instructions: Add multipart upload, ordered metadata, file retrieval, alt text update if needed, and image deletion.
Acceptance Criteria: JPEG, PNG, and WebP work within the configured limit; invalid files fail safely.

Detailed Instructions: Generate API documentation for schemas, CRUD endpoints, image upload, language codes, and error responses.
Acceptance Criteria: The complete API is inspectable and testable in Swagger UI.

Detailed Instructions: Test validation, mapping, slug normalization, service rules, and upload security with JUnit and Mockito where useful.
Acceptance Criteria: Core business rules have deterministic passing tests.

Detailed Instructions: Use Testcontainers PostgreSQL for Flyway, repositories, and REST integration tests instead of relying on H2 compatibility.
Acceptance Criteria: CRUD and upload integration tests pass against disposable PostgreSQL.

Detailed Instructions: Scaffold the frontend with Vite and remove demonstration code.
Acceptance Criteria: npm run dev shows a minimal application without browser console errors.

Detailed Instructions: Install Tailwind and its Vite plugin, import it in the global stylesheet, and define a small accessible theme.
Acceptance Criteria: Tailwind utility classes compile and render.

Detailed Instructions: Add React Router, TanStack Query, React Hook Form, Zod, Hook Form resolver, and React Markdown.
Commands / Files: npm install react-router-dom @tanstack/react-query react-hook-form zod @hookform/resolvers react-markdown
Acceptance Criteria: Dependencies and lockfile are committed and the app builds.

Detailed Instructions: Add Vitest, Testing Library, user-event, MSW, Playwright, and accessibility tooling.
Acceptance Criteria: A sample unit test and Playwright installation check pass.

Detailed Instructions: Enable strict TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, format-check, lint, typecheck, unit-test, and production-build scripts.
Acceptance Criteria: npm run lint, npm run typecheck, and npm run build pass.

Detailed Instructions: Organize API, components, features, hooks, pages, routes, schemas, types, and utilities; keep server state in TanStack Query.
Acceptance Criteria: Every concern has a clear location and no global state library is required.

Detailed Instructions: Create /, /elements/new, /elements/:id, /elements/:id/edit, and not-found routes with a shared accessible layout.
Acceptance Criteria: Direct links and browser back/forward work for every page.

Detailed Instructions: Create typed fetch helpers, common error parsing, base-URL configuration, and multipart upload support.
Acceptance Criteria: The client handles success, field errors, 404, conflict, and network failure.

Detailed Instructions: Use an EN/DE/RU UI message catalogue for labels and errors; store definition translations only in PostgreSQL and persist the selected UI language.
Acceptance Criteria: Interface labels and definition content can change language independently.

Detailed Instructions: Show localized title, slug, and updated date with loading, empty, and error states plus create/edit/delete controls.
Acceptance Criteria: Every stored element appears and actions work by keyboard.

Detailed Instructions: Add title/slug search and basic sorting; keep it client-side initially and document when server pagination should replace it.
Acceptance Criteria: Search and sorting are predictable and clearing controls restores the list.

Detailed Instructions: Show a confirmation dialog containing the title, prevent duplicate submissions, report errors, and refresh cached queries after success.
Acceptance Criteria: Cancel preserves the record; confirm deletes it exactly once.

Detailed Instructions: Render the selected language title, safe Markdown content, examples, ordered responsive images, and edit/back actions.
Acceptance Criteria: Selecting a list row opens the complete detail page.

Detailed Instructions: Create friendly states for missing elements, incomplete translations, broken images, and API failures.
Acceptance Criteria: Every failure has a useful message and a recovery or navigation action.

Detailed Instructions: Create a Zod schema matching backend rules and a reusable form with English, German, and Russian tabs that reveal tab-specific errors.
Acceptance Criteria: Client and server constraints agree and all translations are editable.

Detailed Instructions: Build creation for slug, three translations, Markdown, and examples; prevent duplicate submission and navigate to the created detail.
Acceptance Criteria: A valid definition is created and validation errors appear by the correct fields.

Detailed Instructions: Load existing data, update all translations, preserve unchanged images, and warn about unsaved form changes where appropriate.
Acceptance Criteria: Updates persist and appear immediately on the detail page.

Detailed Instructions: Use the same renderer for preview and detail; keep raw HTML disabled unless a sanitization policy is deliberately added.
Acceptance Criteria: Preview matches saved output and cannot execute scripts.

Detailed Instructions: Support image selection, upload progress, preview, alt text, ordering, deletion, and visible file validation.
Acceptance Criteria: Images can be managed from the editor and appear correctly on detail.

Detailed Instructions: Check semantic headings, table/form labels, keyboard use, focus styles, dialog focus management, alt text, contrast, and reduced-motion behavior.
Commands / Files: All frontend views; automated a11y checks
Acceptance Criteria: No serious automated findings and the full keyboard flow succeeds.

Detailed Instructions: Make tables/actions usable on phones and keep forms, cards, Markdown, and galleries readable at phone, tablet, and desktop widths.
Acceptance Criteria: Key pages have no unintended horizontal overflow.

Detailed Instructions: Test list states, routing, confirmation, language switching, Markdown rendering, form validation, and submissions with mocked HTTP responses.
Acceptance Criteria: Critical flows and failure states have passing component tests.

Detailed Instructions: Test create, list, view, language switch, edit, image upload, persistence after reload, and delete against the full stack.
Acceptance Criteria: The complete requested workflow passes in a browser.

Detailed Instructions: Restrict CORS, cap payloads/uploads, verify MIME and file signatures where practical, sanitize filenames, protect Markdown rendering, and suppress internal errors.
Acceptance Criteria: Tests reject unsafe origins, paths, files, and rendered scripts.

Detailed Instructions: For local-only use, document the absence of access control; before public exposure, protect write operations with authentication and authorization.
Acceptance Criteria: The exposure model is explicit and no unprotected public editor is deployed.

Detailed Instructions: Use a multi-stage build, non-root runtime user, compact Java runtime, environment-based configuration, and Actuator health check.
Acceptance Criteria: The backend image builds and becomes healthy.

Detailed Instructions: Build static assets in one stage and serve them from a small web server with SPA route fallback and API routing/configuration.
Acceptance Criteria: The image builds and nested routes survive direct navigation.

Detailed Instructions: Add frontend and backend services, health-based dependencies, environment variables, PostgreSQL volume, and persistent upload volume.
Acceptance Criteria: docker compose up --build starts the complete app from a clean checkout.

Detailed Instructions: Provide documented start, stop, logs, test, and build commands. Any reset/clean command must not erase persistent data unexpectedly.
Acceptance Criteria: A developer can operate the project without remembering internal commands.

Detailed Instructions: Document prerequisites, WSL setup, environment variables, development mode, Compose mode, migrations, tests, uploads, troubleshooting, and safe data reset.
Acceptance Criteria: A new developer starts the app using only the README.

Detailed Instructions: Describe the data model, API examples, language behavior, image limits, error format, and OpenAPI location.
Acceptance Criteria: Frontend/backend contracts are understandable without reading implementation code.

Detailed Instructions: Run unit tests, PostgreSQL integration tests, packaging, and configured static analysis from a clean state.
Acceptance Criteria: Maven verify completes without failures.

Detailed Instructions: Use a clean install, then run formatting, lint, type checking, unit tests, and production build.
Commands / Files: cd frontend; npm ci; npm run format:check; npm run lint; npm run typecheck; npm test -- --run; npm run build
Acceptance Criteria: Every frontend quality command succeeds.

Detailed Instructions: Start a fresh Compose stack, wait for health checks, run Playwright, and inspect all service logs.
Commands / Files: docker compose up -d --build; Playwright command; docker compose logs
Acceptance Criteria: Browser tests pass and logs contain no unexpected errors.

Detailed Instructions: Clone or copy into a clean WSL environment, configure .env from the example, start the stack, and open the documented URL.
Commands / Files: git clone; cp .env.example .env; docker compose up --build
Acceptance Criteria: No undocumented manual fix is required.

Detailed Instructions: Create EN/DE/RU content with examples/images, find it, view every language, edit it, restart services, verify persistence, and delete it.
Acceptance Criteria: All requested functionality works and data persists across restart.

Detailed Instructions: Test invalid forms, duplicate slug, missing record, backend outage, invalid/large image, and container/database restart.
Acceptance Criteria: Failures are clear, do not corrupt data, and recover when dependencies return.

Detailed Instructions: Check the diff and ensure no credentials, uploads, database files, IDE data, logs, dependencies, or build output are committed.
Commands / Files: git status; git diff; optional secret scanner
Acceptance Criteria: Only intentional source, tests, migrations, templates, and documentation are tracked.

Detailed Instructions: Write release notes, document known limitations, and tag the reproducible first release after acceptance.
Acceptance Criteria: Version 0.1.0 can be rebuilt and its limitations are explicit.

Detailed Instructions: Consider roles/authentication, S3-compatible storage, server pagination/search, audit history, backups, CI/CD, and additional languages after MVP acceptance.
Acceptance Criteria: Future work is separate and does not delay the MVP.
